scope_note: DISCUSSIONS-axis spine for telegram-llm-bot, mined via the discussions-surface lens (gaps users asked about that never got closed (GitHub discussions, unanswered, upvote+comment-weighted)) from ['AstrBot', 'LangBot']. Does NOT predict project-specific product direction — that is strategy, not completeness. An axis gates only after beating the generic-baseline control (check.py VALIDATED_GATING_AXES); the rest are advisory.

required.what: Users hit opaque failures when connecting relay, local, or third-party LLM providers despite configuration tests passing; docs need provider-specific compatibility and error-debug guidance.
required.day1_tell: Follow the documented setup for one relay provider, one local provider, and one third-party provider; intentionally trigger a failed chat request after each config test passes and confirm the docs explain the provider-specific compatibility limits, likely error cause, and debug steps.

required.what: Users encounter unexplained differences across chat surfaces such as group @ replies, private chat, official accounts, personal WeChat, Enterprise WeChat files, and admin identity configuration.
required.day1_tell: Test each supported chat adapter surface on day 1—group @ reply, private chat, official account, personal WeChat, Enterprise WeChat file upload, and admin identity setup—and confirm the docs state the expected behavior, permission requirements, and known differences for each.

required.what: Users lack clear guidance for plugin discovery, installed-plugin introspection, publishing, updating, and debugging custom plugins that fail to run.
required.day1_tell: Install a sample plugin, list installed plugins from the product UI/CLI/API, update it, publish or package it, then break it intentionally and confirm the docs explain discovery, introspection, publishing, updating, logs, and debugging steps.

required.what: Voice, TTS, and chat-file handling are under-documented, with users unsure when conversion, triggering, file retrieval, or platform support should work.
required.day1_tell: Configure voice input, TTS output, and chat-file handling on a supported platform; send a voice message and a file, then confirm the docs explain required conversion services, trigger conditions, retrieval behavior, and platform support limits.

optional.what: Users ask how to make tools, search, embeddings, or local/vector providers work, revealing gaps in capability matrix and setup recipes.
optional.day1_tell: Enable one tool/function call, one search capability, and one embedding/vector provider using only the docs, then run a prompt that should invoke each and confirm the docs include a capability matrix plus working setup recipes and troubleshooting.

optional.category: Response formatting and runtime behavior controls
optional.what: Users cannot predict or control behaviors like segmented replies, temporary model switching, or time/context handling, suggesting missing behavior semantics documentation.
optional.day1_tell: Send prompts that should produce segmented replies, temporary model switching, and time/context-sensitive answers, then confirm the docs define when each runtime behavior occurs and how users can configure, disable, or predict it.

optional.what: Users need documented support for sub-path reverse proxy deployment, static/API routing, and expected URL base configuration.
optional.day1_tell: Deploy the product behind a reverse proxy at a non-root sub-path such as /bot, open the UI, call the API, and load static assets; confirm the docs specify the required base URL, static routing, API routing, and proxy headers.
